method: Visual comparison at the painting camera; hand-read water-contact curves, tree-root rows and distant crest contours. Hidden depth remains interpreted.

observations.difference: The grey-green revision lost the iconic mineral color separation.
observations.change: Restore azurite-blue crests and malachite-green faces; retain warm earth, olive water and light brown paper.

observations.difference: Tree distribution read as paired avenues and a random foreground forest.
observations.change: Author short curved rows from the source, vary spacing and height, and intersect their roots with terrain.

observations.difference: The lake had become a river corridor with continuous shores.
observations.change: Trace curved promontories and inlets, reopen the foreground and add three distant shoals.

observations.difference: Distant mountain lines were repeated smooth waves with uniform spacing.
observations.change: Trace three separate irregular contours and fade remote towers.

observations.difference: Dense woods and repeated shoreline stones hid the small foreground hills.
observations.change: Reduce lowland trees and stones; reject stones placed out in open water.

observations.difference: A blue hill was located beneath the bridge instead of behind the eastern approach.
observations.change: Move its crest and foot landmarks to the observed location.

remainingDifferences: Mountain faces remain more regular and upright than the layered, leaning painted knuckles.
The right foreground crag needs more pronounced broken shelves and overhangs; the present terrain is a height field.
Village groups remain sparse and evenly arranged compared with the source.
Silk weave and brush deposits are simplified; the rendering is still more uniform than the painting.
